beats.text: Cuba puts 13% of its national income into education. Japan spends just 2.6%.
In Africa, Botswana commits 9.5% of its income to schooling, and Namibia spends 8.9%.
This indicator counts current operating expenditures in education like wages, excluding capital investments.
The USA spends 4.4% of its national income on schools.
Higher spenders include New Zealand at 7.4%, Saudi Arabia at 7.2%, Sweden at 7.1%, and Costa Rica at 6.9%.
Near the bottom, Nigeria dedicates 0.8% of its national income to classrooms.
How much national income should your country spend on education?
